chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:

Abu Ya'qub informed me, saying: I saw him — meaning Muhammad — before his death at al-'Askar in the evening, and he had received Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, so he looked toward him, and he fell ill the next day. Then I entered upon him to visit him during his illness after some days, while his condition had become severe. So he informed me that he عليه السلام had sent a cloth to him, and he took it, folded it, and placed it beneath his head. He said: Then he was shrouded in it.

Ahmad said: Abu Ya'qub said: I saw Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام with Ibn al-Khadib, and Ibn al-Khadib said to him, 'Go on, may I be your ransom.' So he عليه السلام said to him, 'You are the one who will precede.' Then no more than four days passed until the shackle was placed on the leg of Ibn al-Khadib, then his death was announced.

He said: It is narrated from him that when Ibn al-Khadib pressed him concerning the house that he was seeking from him, he sent word to him: 'I shall surely seat you, by Allah عز وجل, in a position from which no remnant of you will remain.' So Allah عز وجل took him during those days.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu al-Hasan, the Imam referenced in the report
key_terms.أَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Allah Mighty and Majestic took him, meaning caused his death
key_terms.ابْنِ الْخَضِيبِ: Ibn al-Khadib, the person mentioned in the second and third reports
key_terms.الدَّهَقُ: a shackle or restraint placed on the leg
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرِ: al-'Askar, the location where the event took place
key_terms.بِثَوْبٍ: a cloth sent for use before burial
key_terms.فَكُفِّنَ: he was shrouded, referring to burial preparation
key_terms.مَقْعَدًا: a station or position decreed against someone

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith narrate about Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام and the deaths of Muhammad and Ibn al-Khadib?
ai.summary: This report recounts episodes connected to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, including the final illness of Muhammad and a burial cloth sent to him, as well as statements concerning Ibn al-Khadib that were followed by his death. The narration highlights the Imam’s foreknowledge and the unfolding of events surrounding those who encountered him.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from a man, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad who said, ‘Abu Yaqoub Informed me saying,

‘I saw him, meaning Muhammad (Ibn Al-Faraj), before his death at Al-Askar in the evening, and Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> had received him, and he<sup>asws</sup> looked after him, and he became ill the next morning, and I went to console him after a few days from his illness and it has become worse. So he informed me that he<sup>asws</sup> had sent a cloth to him, so he took it and layered it and placed it under his head. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he was enshrouded in it.

Ahmad said, ‘Abu Yaqoub said, ‘I saw Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (10<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) with Ibn Al-Khazeyb, so Ibn Al-Khazeyb said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘(You<sup>asws</sup> will) go (first), May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘You would be the preceding one’. So it was not long except for four days until shackles were placed upon the leg of Ibn Al-Khazeyb, then news of his death was released’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘It is reported from him when Ibn Al-Kahzeyb insisted upon him<sup>asws</sup> regarding the house which he was seeking from him<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> sent a message to him: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> shall sit with you from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic with such a sitting that there will not remain for you a remaining (trace)’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Seized him during that year’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali who has said the following.

“Muhammad ibn al-Faraj told me that abu al-Hassan (a.s.) has written to him this. “O Muhammad, organize you affairs and be careful.” He said that he began to organize his affairs and did not know what the Imam (a.s.) meant thereby until police came to me and took me out of Egypt as a captive. All of my belongings were confiscated and I remained in prison for eight years. In the prison I received a letter from him that said, “O Muhammad, do not reside in the western location.” I read the letter and said to my self, “He writes me this and I am in prison. This is strange.” Shortly afterwards, I was released, thanks to Allah. The narrator has said that Muhammad ibn al-Faraj wrote to him about his properties. The Imam (a.s.) wrote to him in response, “Your properties will soon be returned to you and even if they are not returned to you it will not harm you.” When Muhammad al-Faraj left to the army camp (Samarra) an order was issued to release his properties but he died before receiving them.

The narrator has said that Ahmad ibn al-Khadib wrote to Muhammad ibn al-Faraj asking him to come to the army camp. He wrote to the Imam (a.s.) for his advise in the matter and the response was this. “ Go out. In it there will be happiness and relief for you, by the will of Allah, the Most High..” He left for the journey but very shortly afterwards he died.”
